subject: physics
title: Waves Adventure 1: Wave properties and v = fλ
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet transverse and longitudinal waves and use v = fλ.
meta_desc: Physics — wave types, transverse vs longitudinal, frequency, wavelength, v = fλ.
final_note: You learned waves transfer energy without matter, transverse waves oscillate ⊥ to motion (light, water), longitudinal ∥ (sound), and v = fλ.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Transverse: oscillation ⊥ direction of travel. Examples: water surface, EM waves (light, radio), seismic S-waves.

Longitudinal: oscillation parallel. Examples: sound, seismic P-waves. Compressions and rarefactions.

v = f · λ

f in Hz (1/s), λ in m, v in m/s.

Sound in air: v ≈ 340 m/s.
Light in vacuum: c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.

Period T = 1/f.

Wavefronts: lines of equal phase (e.g. crests).
Rays: arrows perpendicular to wavefronts, showing direction.

Reflection: angle in = angle out.
Refraction: v changes → λ changes (f unchanged); ray bends.
Snell: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂.
